title: Fine-tuning methods: SFT, DPO, RFT and LoRA
summary: SFT learns from correct answers, DPO from preferred and rejected pairs, RFT from a grader, and LoRA is a cheap way to train adapters. Platform availability is the first question.
useIf: You need a consistent format, tone, tool-use behaviour or a smaller model and you have examples.
avoidIf: You want to add facts or current information. Evidence favours retrieval for that.

explain.md: **SFT** (supervised fine-tuning) trains on input and ideal-output examples. OpenAI needs at least 10 examples, often sees gains at 50 to 100, and lists the `gpt-4.1` family [[r52]]. **DPO** (direct preference optimization) trains on preferred and rejected pairs with a `beta` between 0 and 2, where higher stays closer to the base model. It replaces the RLHF reward model and RL loop with a classification loss [[r53]] [[r46]]. **RFT** (reinforcement fine-tuning) scores outputs with a grader you write, and OpenAI lists `o4-mini` only [[r54]].

**LoRA** freezes the weights and trains small low-rank matrices. Against full Adam fine-tuning of GPT-3 175B it cut trainable parameters 10,000 times and GPU memory 3 times, with no added inference latency [[r45]]. **QLoRA** fine-tunes a 65B model on one 48GB GPU using 4-bit NormalFloat, double quantization and paged optimizers [[r25]]. These are paper results, not product limits.

explain.title: Which method for which signal
explain.alt: Decision flow: if you need facts use retrieval; otherwise choose SFT with correct answers, DPO with preference pairs, RFT with a reliable grader, or LoRA and QLoRA for open weights you host.
explain.src:
flowchart TD
  A[What do you need] -->|Facts| B[RAG or context]
  A -->|Behaviour| C{What signal do you have}
  C -->|Correct answers| D[SFT]
  C -->|Preferred and rejected pairs| E[DPO]
  C -->|A reliable grader| F[RFT]
  C -->|Open weights you host| G[LoRA or QLoRA]

explain.title: OpenAI is winding down self-serve fine-tuning
explain.md: Notice date 2026-05-07. Organisations that never ran fine-tuning cannot create jobs. From 2026-07-02, organisations with no fine-tuned inference in 60 days cannot. On 2027-01-06 active customers can no longer create jobs. Fine-tuned inference ends only when its base model is deprecated, several fine-tuned ids end on 2026-10-23, and the GPT-6 Astra page marks the fine-tuning endpoint unsupported [[r11]].

**Azure** keeps managed SFT, DPO and RFT. Interactive training is Preview and needs approval. Training types are Standard, Data zone (US only), Global and Developer (preemptible, no SLA). Deployment options are Serverless, Managed compute (Preview, LoRA adapters) and Fireworks on Foundry (Preview). Models include the `gpt-4.1` family (SFT, DPO), `gpt-4o` (SFT, DPO), `gpt-4o-mini` (SFT), `o4-mini` (RFT) and open-weight models, with `gpt-5` RFT by invitation only. Training on the `gpt-4.1` family ends no earlier than 2027-04-14 for existing customers [[r17]] [[r13]]. Azure retires `o4-mini`, the RFT model, on 2026-11-19, so plan a replacement [[tr5]].

whereToUse: A strict output format or house style that few-shot prompts follow unreliably
Tool-use habits, such as always calling a tool in a certain situation
Replacing a long few-shot prompt with a tuned smaller model at high volume
Preference alignment, such as concise versus verbose answers (DPO)
Self-hosted open-weight models adapted with LoRA or QLoRA

use: SFT when you can show the right answer and have hundreds of clean examples
DPO when you can compare two outputs but not write the ideal one
RFT when a reliable programmatic grader exists
LoRA or QLoRA when you host open weights and GPU memory is limited
avoid: Fine-tuning to teach facts or keep knowledge current
Tuning on a base model that retires soon without a migration plan
RFT with a noisy or gameable grader
flips: The platform blocks new jobs: use structured outputs and few-shot prompting, or use Azure or open weights
The prompt baseline already meets the bar: do not tune
Data is small and noisy: improve data or prompts before tuning

pitfalls.symptom: A new organisation cannot start a fine-tuning job on OpenAI
pitfalls.cause: Since 2026-05-07 orgs that never ran fine-tuning cannot create jobs
pitfalls.fix: Check eligibility first, or use Azure, open weights or prompting

pitfalls.symptom: The tuned model repeats old facts
pitfalls.cause: Facts were trained into weights and the source changed
pitfalls.fix: Keep facts in retrieval and tune behaviour only

pitfalls.symptom: A tuned model disappears from a deployment plan
pitfalls.cause: Fine-tuned inference ends when its base model is deprecated
pitfalls.fix: Record the base-model retirement date and schedule a re-tune

pitfalls.symptom: RFT improves the grader score and not the task
pitfalls.cause: The grader is gameable or measures a proxy
pitfalls.fix: Audit the grader on held-out samples and add checks

scenarios.title: A new team wants SFT for a format task
scenarios.situation: A team with no fine-tuning history on the OpenAI API has 1,500 approved examples and wants a model that always produces a five-section report. There is no hard platform constraint.
constraints: No prior fine-tuning on OpenAI direct
unknowns: Does a strict schema plus few-shot prompting already meet the bar?
When does the candidate base model retire?
scenarios.question: What is the plan?

options.name: Run SFT on Azure Foundry on a supported model after confirming its retirement date, and keep a prompt baseline to beat
options.why: The need is format with data in hand, and Azure offers managed SFT while OpenAI blocks new organisations [[r17]] [[r11]].
options.tradeoff: Training effort, a retirement date to track (`gpt-4.1` training ends no earlier than 2027-04-14) and a re-tune later.

options.name: Use structured outputs and a few-shot prompt, and skip training
options.why: Nothing to train or retire, and may already pass.
options.tradeoff: Longer prompts and weaker format consistency at volume.

options.name: Plan on OpenAI fine-tuning next quarter
options.why: Organisations that never ran fine-tuning have been blocked from creating jobs since 2026-05-07.
options.tradeoff: It remains valid for orgs with eligible fine-tuning history.

flips.if: The prompt baseline already meets the bar
Data must stay in a specific region
flips.then: Pick the Azure training type that matches residency.

scenarios.takeaway: Check platform availability and the baseline before you collect data.

scenarios.title: Shifting style from rater preferences
scenarios.situation: Raters compared pairs of answers and chose the better one in 2,000 cases. There is no ideal answer for each prompt, and quality is subjective.
unknowns: Which base model is supported for DPO?
scenarios.question: Which method fits?

options.name: SFT on the chosen answers only
options.why: Easy to run and uses part of the signal.
options.tradeoff: It discards the rejected examples that teach what to avoid.

options.name: DPO on the pairs, tuning `beta`
options.why: It uses the preferred and rejected signal directly, and `beta` controls how far the model moves from the base [[r53]].
options.tradeoff: Pair quality matters and results need an eval set.

options.name: RFT with a grader
options.why: Subjective quality has no reliable programmatic grader, so the model may chase the grader.
options.tradeoff: RFT suits tasks with checkable answers, such as structured correctness.

flips.then: RFT becomes an option on supported models.

scenarios.takeaway: Match the method to the signal you have.

scenarios.title: Adapting an open-weight model on one GPU
scenarios.situation: A team hosts an open-weight 65B model and has one 48GB GPU. They need domain-specific behaviour and cannot send data to a hosted API.
unknowns: Is a 4-bit base acceptable for quality?
scenarios.question: How do you train it?

options.name: Full fine-tuning of all weights
options.why: It needs far more memory than a single 48GB GPU provides for a 65B model.
options.tradeoff: Full tuning suits a small model or a large cluster.

options.name: LoRA on a 16-bit base
options.why: Adapters cut trainable parameters and memory.
options.tradeoff: The 16-bit base itself may not fit a single 48GB GPU at this size.

options.name: QLoRA with a 4-bit base
options.why: It fine-tuned a 65B model on one 48GB GPU in the paper, with LoRA adapters [[r25]].
options.tradeoff: Paper results are not a product guarantee, and 4-bit quantization may cost some quality.

flips.then: LoRA on a higher-precision base is an option.

flips.if: Data may go to a managed service

scenarios.takeaway: QLoRA trades some precision for fitting big models on small GPUs.

quiz.q: Match each method to the signal it needs.

pairs.r: A 4-bit base with LoRA adapters on limited GPU memory

quiz.explain: Each method consumes a different training signal. LoRA and QLoRA are parameter-efficient ways to train, and are not signals themselves.

quiz.q: A team that never ran fine-tuning on the OpenAI API tries to create a job and is refused. Why?
options: OpenAI wound down self-serve fine-tuning for orgs without prior use, from 2026-05-07
The model is unsupported by SFT
Jobs need an invitation on every platform
quiz.explain: Notice date 2026-05-07: organisations that never ran fine-tuning cannot create jobs. Dataset size and model support are separate issues, and Azure offers managed methods.

quiz.q: LoRA cut trainable parameters 10,000 times against full Adam fine-tuning of GPT-3 175B. Roughly how many parameters does that leave to train?
quiz.explain: 175,000,000,000 divided by 10,000 is 17,500,000 trainable parameters. The ratio is a paper result for that setup, not a general constant.

flashcards.front: When do you choose DPO over SFT?
flashcards.back: When you have preferred and rejected pairs but no single ideal answer per prompt. `beta` (0 to 2) sets how far the model moves from the base.

flashcards.front: What did the QLoRA paper show?
flashcards.back: A 65B model fine-tuned on one 48GB GPU using 4-bit NormalFloat, double quantization and paged optimizers.

flashcards.front: When does OpenAI stop new fine-tuning jobs for active customers?
flashcards.back: 2027-01-06. Fine-tuned inference ends when the base model is deprecated.

flashcards.front: Which methods does Azure offer for managed fine-tuning?
flashcards.back: SFT, DPO and RFT, with Standard, Data zone, Global and Developer training types.
